verdicts.title: Multiparty Karchmer-Wigderson Games and Threshold Circuits
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We suggest a generalization of Karchmer-Wigderson communication games to the multiparty setting. Our generalization turns out to be tightly connected to circuits consisting of threshold gates. This allows us to obtain new explicit constructions of such circuits for several functions. In particular, we provide an explicit (polynomial-time computable) log-depth monotone formula for Majority function, consisting only of 3-bit majority gates and variables. This resolves a conjecture of Cohen et al.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract discusses a multiparty generalization of Karchmer-Wigderson games connected to threshold circuits and constructs a monotone formula for Majority, but says nothing about polynomial threshold function degree, CNF representations of PARITY, or an Ω(log n) lower bound.

verdicts.title: Karchmer-Wigderson Games for Hazard-free Computation
verdicts.abstract_excerpt:
We present a Karchmer-Wigderson game to study the complexity of hazard-free formulas. This new game is both a generalization of the monotone Karchmer-Wigderson game and an analog of the classical Boolean Karchmer-Wigderson game. Therefore, it acts as a bridge between the existing monotone and general games.

verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract focuses on Karchmer-Wigderson games for hazard-free formula complexity (size/depth lower bounds, multiplexer constructions), not on polynomial threshold function degree bounds for CNF formulas computing PARITY. It shares the KW framework vocabulary but does not address PTF degree or PARITY.

verdicts.title: The degree of the Alexander polynomial is an upper bound for the topological slice genus
verdicts.abstract_excerpt: We use the famous knot-theoretic consequence of Freedman's disc theorem---knots with trivial Alexander polynomial bound a locally-flat disc in the 4-ball---to prove the following generalization. The degree of the Alexander polynomial of a knot is an upper bound for twice its topological slice genus. We provide examples of knots where this determines the topological slice genus.
verdicts.judge_reasoning: The abstract concerns the Alexander polynomial of knots and topological slice genus in knot theory ('degree of the Alexander polynomial...upper bound for twice its topological slice genus'), which has no interaction with polynomial threshold functions or PARITY complexity.
